articles.title: Bjarke Ingels Group Designs Timber Residential and Hotel Project in Thun
articles.excerpt: Bjarke Ingels Group has unveiled plans for four timber-focused buildings combining hotels and residences for the new Siegenthalergut district in Thun, Switzerland.
articles.content: Bjarke Ingels Group has announced Nachwachsende Stadt, a four-building timber development designed for the western entrance of the Siegenthalergut district in Thun, Switzerland. Selected through a competition organized by Frutiger AG and the city of Thun, the 13,000-square-meter scheme combines a multi-star hotel structure with residential blocks featuring flexible layouts. The proposal, developed alongside landscape architects August + Margrith Künzel, incorporates stepped facades with deep window grids, terraces overlooking the Bernese Alps, and an internal courtyard with garden paths. Designed for future disassembly to reduce embodied carbon, the timber structures integrate rainwater retention systems and approximately 1,800 square meters of photovoltaic panels. Targeting Switzerland's SNBS Gold sustainability certification, the project is slated to advance through further design stages, with construction potentially beginning in 2028.

articles.originalTitle: Mary Miss’s Long Fight to Keep Public Art Alive - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Mary Miss and Her Long Career Shaping the Boundaries of Public Art
articles.excerpt: Pioneering public artist Mary Miss reflects on decades of creating site-specific works that challenge conventional definitions of art, architecture, and landscape in the modern world.
articles.content: Born in 1944, Mary Miss emerged as a pioneering figure in the public art revolution of the 1980s, moving away from static monuments toward participatory installations. Among her most celebrated works is South Cove, a waterside park created between 1984 and 1987 in Manhattan's Battery Park City, which integrated natural elements with maritime history. Throughout a career spanning decades, Miss encountered bureaucratic obstacles, budget limitations, nonpayment, and the dismantling of signature pieces. Rather than deterring her, these challenges prompted her to adapt her approach, culminating in ongoing community-focused initiatives such as her City as Living Laboratory project. From her early outdoor constructions in Colorado to urban interventions that incorporated deep site research, her practice consistently challenged conventional definitions of public art. Her 1977 installation Perimeters, Pavilions, Decoys notably helped shape critical discourse regarding sculpture in the expanded field, engaging directly with architecture and landscape. Despite shifts in public funding and political climates, Miss maintains a steadfast dedication to fostering connections and dialogue through art created specifically for public spaces.

articles.originalTitle: EU Countries Renew Call To Exclude Russia from Venice Ahead of 2027 Architecture Biennale - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Ten European Union Countries Renew Demands to Exclude Russia From Venice Architecture Biennale
articles.excerpt: Ten EU nations have urged the European Commission to prevent Russia's participation in the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale, arguing that Moscow's presence risks normalizing the war in Ukraine.
articles.content: Ten European Union nations are demanding sustained efforts from the European Commission to keep Russia out of the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale. According to a diplomatic note signed by Poland, Austria, Croatia, Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Germany, Latvia, Lithuania, and Sweden, Moscow's presence on the cultural stage risks normalizing its war in Ukraine. The group urged measures ahead of a meeting of EU culture ministers. Russia returned to the Venice Biennale in May for the first time since its 2022 invasion of Ukraine, drawing widespread condemnation. The European Commission previously withdrew a 2 million euro grant after Biennale organizers rejected calls to exclude Moscow. The May exhibition faced protests from dissident groups and temporary pavilion closures across multiple participating countries. Biennale president Pietrangelo Buttafuoco defended the decision, maintaining that the independent institution rejects the exclusion of culture and art. The 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale is scheduled to run from May 8 to November 21, curated by Wang Shu and Lu Wenyu.

articles.originalTitle: Nan Goldin to debut new film exploring nature and extinction in first UK solo museum show in over two decades - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Nan Goldin Debuts Nature-Focused Film in First UK Solo Show in Decades
articles.excerpt: American photographer Nan Goldin is premiering new films exploring nature, extinction, and animals at London's Hayward Gallery. The exhibition marks her first institutional solo show in the United Kingdom in over twenty years.
articles.content:
American photographer Nan Goldin is opening her first institutional solo exhibition in the United Kingdom in over twenty years at London's Hayward Gallery. Running from 24 November to 14 March 2027, the exhibition expands Goldin's compassionate lens from human relationships and queer communities toward the natural world and ecological themes. Four years in the making, the show forms part of the Southbank Centre's 75th-anniversary programme.

The exhibition's centrepiece is the premiere of You never did anything wrong, Part II (2026), created alongside film-maker David Sherman. The work draws upon 1960s and 70s nature documentaries and damaged soundtracks to present an abstract meditation on animals, land, and impending extinction. It accompanies the 2024 first part, which centres on a solar eclipse. The presentation also includes Stendhal Syndrome, pairing portraits of friends with classical art, and Memory Lost, which addresses addiction and Goldin's activism through the Prescription Addiction Intervention Now group.

articles.originalTitle: Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires – exhibition large print guide - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: Victoria and Albert Museum Publishes Constantinople Exhibition Guide
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum has published a comprehensive exhibition guide examining the rich history, art, and architecture of the city that served as capital to two empires.
articles.content: The Victoria and Albert Museum has issued an exhibition guide detailing the historical transformation from Constantinople to Istanbul. In 324 CE, Emperor Constantine I selected the ancient site as his new capital, naming it Nova Roma before it became known as Constantinople. The settlement served as the capital of the Byzantine Empire until 1453, and subsequently as the Ottoman capital until 1922. Situated at the junction of Asia and Europe, the metropolis flourished through trade, taxation, and loot, funding outstanding public works and architecture. The exhibition explores the city's vital engineering feats, including the 5.6-kilometer Theodosian Walls and the 4th-century Aqueduct of Valens. Religious life transitioned through Roman paganism, Christianity, and Islam, while a diverse population of merchants and craftspeople inhabited the urban center. The guide highlights various historical objects, such as ivory plaques of Christ Pantocrator, Hâfız Osman's calligraphy describing the Prophet Muhammad, restoration inscriptions of Emperor Michael III, and cameos made from rock crystal, lapis lazuli, and amethyst. These artifacts demonstrate the two distinct traditions of art and design practiced within the city across its long imperial history.

articles.originalTitle: 2026 Record Awards: Jules & Jim Bridges by Dietmar Feichtinger Architects - Architectural Record
articles.title: New Pedestrian Bridges Reconnect Historic Centers Across the Seine Near Paris
articles.excerpt: Designed by Dietmar Feichtinger Architectes, the Jules and Jim bridges restore a historic link destroyed in World War II, creating a continuous pedestrian and bicycle route connecting Mantes-la-Jolie and Limay.
articles.content: Constructed over the Seine River in France, a pair of pedestrian footbridges named Jules and Jim reconnect the historic centers of Mantes-la-Jolie and Limay. Located about 30 miles west of Paris, the project restores a link lost with the destruction of a medieval bridge during World War II. The design introduces two contemporary crossings, establishing a continuous pedestrian and bicycle route connecting public spaces, parks, and cultural landmarks. The 660-foot Jules bridge spans from Mantes to the Île aux Dames in the middle of the river, utilizing existing masonry piers of the adjacent vehicular crossing to minimize riverbed disruption. The 80-foot Jim bridge connects the island and Limay by spanning extant sections of the medieval crossing. Named after a 1962 film by François Truffaut, the project transforms a historical rupture into a renewed connection. The client for the initiative is the Syndicat Mixte d’aménagement, de gestion et d’entretien des berges de la Seine et Oise. Dietmar Feichtinger Architectes served as the architect, with engineering by Terrell SAS, historic monument consulting by ALEP Architectes, and lighting design by Coup d’éclat.

articles.originalTitle: Parthenon’s east pediment, ‘the most famous image of antiquity’, recreated in Frankfurt exhibition - The Art Newspaper
articles.title: Parthenon's East Pediment Recreated in Frankfurt Exhibition Following Decades of Research
articles.excerpt: The Liebieghaus Sculpture Collection in Frankfurt has reconstructed the destroyed east pediment of the Parthenon using reliefs from Roman sarcophagi lids. The research findings are now on display in a new exhibition.
articles.content:
The Liebieghaus Sculpture Collection in Frankfurt has reconstructed the destroyed east pediment of the Parthenon, depicting the birth of Athena, following decades of research. Running from 18 November to 25 July 2027, the exhibition showcases the central sculpted ensemble of the ancient temple.

The research team achieved a breakthrough by investigating figural reliefs on nine Roman sarcophagi lids housed in institutions including the State Hermitage Museum and the Vatican Museums. Utilizing computer technology, the team established a complete match between these reliefs and the remaining fragments of the pediment. The findings revealed previously unknown figures on the pediment, including the Dioscuri horsemen responding to the cosmic cataclysm of Athena's birth.

Prior to the opening, political tensions surfaced regarding loan agreements. The Greek government withdrew its loan of nine marble fragments from the Acropolis Museum because they were to be displayed alongside British Museum pieces. Meanwhile, the British Museum confirmed it would proceed with lending two fragments to the exhibition, which highlights findings based primarily on decades of Liebieghaus research.

articles.originalTitle: Construction underway on Jean Nouvel’s landmark opera house in China - Dezeen
articles.title: Construction Work Continues on the Shenzhen Opera House in China
articles.excerpt: Designed by French architecture studio Ateliers Jean Nouvel and built in Shenzhen, China, the new opera house is scheduled for completion in 2028.
articles.content: French architecture studio Ateliers Jean Nouvel has released construction photographs of the Shenzhen Opera House located on the Shekou Peninsula in China. Spanning 250,000 square meters, the cultural landmark is scheduled for completion in 2028. The design, which won an international architecture competition, features an elongated, wavy roofscape reflecting the site's connection to the bay. Conceived by Pritzker Prize-winning architect Jean Nouvel, the facility includes a 2,300-seat concert hall with a horseshoe-shaped plan, an 1,800-seat theatre, and an 800-seat venue. Additional facilities comprise a 400-seat multifunctional theatre, cultural spaces, backstage areas, offices, and performers' apartments. To connect the interior architecture with the surrounding water, iridescent materials such as mother-of-pearl are planned for the interior surfaces. The published construction images visualize the substantial scale of the waterfront development and its performance halls.

articles.originalTitle: Yayoi Kusama ‘Infinity Net’ Painting Sells for $15.1 M. at Sotheby’s, Setting a Record - ARTnews.com
articles.title: Yayoi Kusama Painting Sets New Auction Record at Sotheby's
articles.excerpt: A 1960 "Infinity Net" painting by Yayoi Kusama sold for $15.1 million at Sotheby's in New York, setting a new auction record for the artist.
articles.content: Just months after the death of Yayoi Kusama, her 1960 painting titled No. 3P.B. sold at a Sotheby's auction in New York for a hammer price of $12.5 million, reaching $15.1 million with fees to set a new auction record for the artist. The work sold following a brief bidding war conducted by phone representatives over the course of four minutes across 10 bids. The hammer price placed the canvas squarely within its presale estimate of $10 million to $15 million. Standing over five feet tall, the crimson canvas is an early example of Kusama's large-scale monochrome abstractions covered in thousands of looping brushstrokes known as the "Infinity Net" series. Later in the same evening, another painting from the series, dating to 2011, sold for $3.06 million with fees. Since Kusama passed away in August at the age of 97, nearly 30 of her works have appeared at major auction houses. Her previous record was established in 2022 by a white "Infinity Net" painting that achieved $10.5 million with fees at Phillips New York.

articles.originalTitle: Dezeen Awards 2026 architecture project of the year revealed - Dezeen
articles.title: Tree-Top Sauna Named Architecture Project of the Year at Dezeen Awards 2026
articles.excerpt: Located in a Kanagawa forest, the Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna has been named architecture project of the year at the ninth Dezeen Awards, praised for integrating architecture with nature.
articles.content: Nineteen architecture category winners across 11 countries were announced at the ninth annual Dezeen Awards ceremony in London. Situated within a forest in Kanagawa, the Daichi Silent River Tree Sauna claimed both the leisure and wellness category win and the overall project of the year award. The master jury commended the minimalist, biophilic project for its spiritual touch. Additionally, Amami House on Amami Ōshima won urban house of the year for sustainable off-grid living, while Jiang Deng Lu in China took the rural house prize. La Querola in Andorra won housing project of the year, Zando Central Market in Kinshasa won the civic category, and the Ismaili Center in Houston secured the cultural project award. The winning designs highlighted sustainable material use, local craft traditions, and community engagement across global contexts.

articles.originalTitle: Construction Starts on $246M Niagara Falls Power Station Hotel Conversion - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Historic Niagara Falls Power Station Converted Into Luxury Hotel
articles.excerpt: Construction has begun on a privately financed redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to convert the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station near Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex, with completion expected in 2029.
articles.content: Construction has commenced on a redevelopment exceeding 246 million dollars to transform the century-old Toronto Power Generating Station overlooking Niagara Falls into a hotel and visitor complex. Owned by the Ontario provincial agency Niagara Parks, the historic facility is being redeveloped by Toronto Power Hotel Inc., a partnership overseeing the privately financed project. Deltera Contracting Inc. serves as the general contractor, with +VG Architects and MT Planners on the project team. Designed by E.J. Lennox, the steel-frame building opened in 1906 and operated until 1974. The preservation effort will maintain key architectural features while adding a five-star hotel, multiple restaurants, a wellness spa, event facilities, an art gallery, a museum, and public viewing areas. Audited financial statements indicate that approximately 6.72 million dollars in stabilization obligations were transferred to Society Land Holdings Inc. under a long-term lease. Substantial construction completion is anticipated in 2029, with the hotel opening scheduled for 2030.

articles.originalTitle: Building a Permanent Home for a Space Shuttle Was an Engineering Endeavor - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Permanent Exhibition Center Unveiled for Retired Space Shuttle Endeavor
articles.excerpt: The 450-million-dollar Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center at the California Science Center in Los Angeles has opened to house the vertically positioned space shuttle Endeavor.
articles.content: The Samuel Oschin Air and Space Center has opened at the California Science Center in Los Angeles, housing the retired space shuttle Endeavor. Having completed its final mission in June 2011, Endeavor is the world's only space shuttle exhibited in the vertical launch configuration, complete with boosters and an external tank. Designed by ZGF Architects and built by general contractor MATT Construction, the 200-foot-tall curvilinear stainless-steel structure required complex seismic analysis and intricate steel node assembly. Engineering teams utilized specialized scaffolding and commercial cranes to maneuver components without damaging the fragile thermal silica tiles on the shuttle. To comply with Exposition Park campus height limits, the facility was designed 25 feet below grade, completing a multi-year effort to establish a permanent home for the spacecraft.

articles.originalTitle: Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA Receives the First Ambasz–MoMA Annual Prize for Nature–Reconciled Architecture - ArchDaily
articles.title: Kashef Chowdhury and URBANA Receive the First Ambasz-MoMA Prize for Nature-Reconciled Architecture
articles.excerpt: The Museum of Modern Art has selected Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA for the inaugural Ambasz-MoMA Annual Prize for Nature-Reconciled Architecture for the Friendship Centre project in Gaibandha. The $200,000 award is shared between the architect and Argentina's Fundación Gran Chaco.
articles.content: The Museum of Modern Art selected Kashef Chowdhury/URBANA for the inaugural Ambasz-MoMA Annual Prize for Nature-Reconciled Architecture for the design of the Friendship Centre, a rural training facility in Gaibandha, Bangladesh. Described by MoMA as the largest award for a single architecture project, the prize aims to recognize architectural practice while supporting environmental action. The $200,000 award is shared between the architect and Fundación Gran Chaco, a nonprofit organization in Formosa, Argentina, to plant trees in the Gran Chaco forest. The project was chosen from nearly 140 international entries by a jury comprising MoMA representatives and external members based on rigor, creative engagement with the natural environment, and alignment with the institute's mission. Completed in 2011, the Friendship Centre responds to seasonal flooding and earthquakes in the Jamuna River delta using a compacted earthen embankment and handcrafted local clay bricks. The layout reflects the nearby third-century BCE ancient city of Mahasthangarh while integrating green roofs and rainwater harvesting pools. The award will be presented during a ceremony at MoMA on December 12, 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Birthday Exhibition at the Paris Mint - WWD
articles.title: Fragonard Hosts Centenary Exhibition at the Paris Mint
articles.excerpt: Grasse-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is opening a centenary exhibition featuring more than 250 works and objects at the Paris Mint.
articles.content: Frane-based fragrance and lifestyle brand Fragonard is celebrating its centenary with a major exhibition at the Paris Mint. Entitled "Fragonard: 100 Years of Collections and Savoir-Faire," the event gathers more than 250 works and objects from the house's heritage collection. The exhibition remains open to the public through Jan. 17, 2027. Company chief executive officer Agnès Costa Webster noted that paintings from the family's collection in Grasse have been brought to Paris for the first time. Hosted at the 18th-century Hôtel de la Monnaie, the multisensory exhibition features paintings, perfume bottles, historic garments, silverware, and personal grooming accessories. The scenography was conceived by Nathalie Crinière, while Givaudan perfumer Daniela Andrier formulated scents based on 18th-century recipes specifically for the event. Visitors can also explore an onsite boutique and attend fragrance-making workshops by reservation.

articles.originalTitle: Eight Dead, 18 Injured in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site - Engineering News-Record
articles.title: Eight Dead in Brooklyn Building Collapse Next to Construction Site
articles.excerpt: Eight people were killed and 18 others injured when a three-story building collapsed into an excavation site in Brooklyn, prompting multiple official investigations.
articles.content: A 96-year-old three-story building collapsed into an adjacent excavation site on Flatbush Avenue in Brooklyn, resulting in eight fatalities, including two children and two construction workers, and 18 injuries. Rescue operations concluded following the incident. A project geotechnical report had previously indicated that abutting structures required underpinning and warned that excavation vibration could adversely affect them. A March preconstruction survey documented visible cracking and rated the north masonry facade poorly. Approved excavation-support plans prescribed specific monitoring thresholds for movement and vibration. Available records do not establish whether the structure was underpinned or what the final monitoring readings showed before the collapse. Mayor Zohran Mamdani ordered safety inspections at approximately 100 other construction sites associated with the project's firms. New York Attorney General Letitia James announced that the Buildings Department would conduct a full investigation, while Brooklyn District Attorney Eric Gonzalez launched a separate inquiry. City records show the development had faced earlier stop-work orders during demolition phases before excavation began.

articles.originalTitle: Designers’ Creative Freedom Unveiled at Molteni Museum Exhibit - WWD
articles.title: Molteni Museum Exhibition Gives Designers Creative Freedom
articles.excerpt: A new exhibition at the Molteni Museum in Giussano, Italy, invites prominent designers and architects to reinterpret existing brand furniture into unique, expressive works of art free from commercial constraints.
articles.content: The Molteni Museum at the Molteni Compound in Giussano, Italy, has launched an exhibition giving living designers and architects the freedom to transform existing brand furniture into unique artistic works without commercial constraints. The showcase features contributions from international practices and creators, including Herzog & de Meuron, Jean Nouvel, Naoto Fukasawa, OMA, AMDL Circle, Foster + Partners Industrial Design, Patricia Urquiola, the late Luca Meda, and Vincent Van Duysen. Herzog & de Meuron reinterpreted a special-edition chair with candy-colored inflatable cushions, while Ron Gilad transformed a kitchen island into a poetic fountain with four faucets as a tribute to Luca Meda. The OMA firm experimented with materials to redesign tables from the Principles collection, and AMDL Circle re-imagined workstation systems into surreal, centipede-like contours. The exhibition will remain on display for one year and is expected to travel internationally.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | TAREK EL-ARISS | Emptying the Jars of War, or How We Learned to Love Nature - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Tarek El-Ariss to Discuss War, Nature, and Water Politics at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Tarek El-Ariss will examine how crises alter perceptions of nature and reframe sustainability during a lecture at Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Tarek El-Ariss is scheduled to speak at an event during Biennale Arte 2026 on November 21, 2026. Taking place at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale from 16:00 to 17:30, the lecture will be introduced and moderated by Rasha Salti. The session addresses how crises and wars not only damage the environment but also unsettle perceptions of nature. Drawing from everyday scenes such as saving water jars for bathing during wartime in Lebanon, the discussion traces longer histories and mythologies of water and greenery from the Garden of Eden to Greek and Islamic traditions, while focusing on the oasis as a recurring fantasy. The lecture posits that environmental practices do not necessarily emerge from ethical choices, often arising instead through habit, fear, or the quest for survival. Sustainability is reframed as a negotiation that interrogates the politics of purity and control to imagine alternative futures. Admission to the event is free until venue capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: FRIEDA EKOTTO | Resilience Against Value: Authored Practices of Repair in Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Frieda Ekotto to Deliver Lecture at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale
articles.excerpt: Frieda Ekotto will deliver a lecture examining the repair practices in the works of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event takes place on November 20, 2026, at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale.
articles.content: Frieda Ekotto will present a lecture examining the gathering, wrapping, repairing, and regenerating actions central to the practices of Otobong Nkanga and Ibrahim Mahama. The event is scheduled for November 20, 2026, from 16:00 to 17:30 at Teatro Piccolo Arsenale. The discussion explores processes that redirect materials, labor, and time toward connections between land, body, and community that extraction seeks to disrupt. These actions form a resilience rooted in acts of refusal. By framing disobedience as the foundation of resilience, the lecture recasts the work of both artists as a sustained challenge to damaging value systems, pointing toward a relational model of authorship. Rasha Salti will introduce and moderate the session. Admission to the venue is free until capacity is reached.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | RANA EL NEMR | The Newborn Birthchart - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Rana El Nemr Presents The Newborn Birthchart at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Rana El Nemr’s two-part installation, The Newborn Birthchart, is presented at the Arsenale during Biennale Arte 2026, inviting audiences to share communal stories and songs.
articles.content: Scheduled for 18 November 2026 from 11:00 to 11:30 at the Arsenale, the performance titled The Newborn Birthchart forms part of Biennale Arte 2026. Designed as an active threshold, the two-part installation registers each visit as a vibrational contribution to the work in space. Through readings, songs, incantations, and cues from the artwork's card deck, the performance invites the audience to communally harvest the stories and songs of swamps, canefields, sugar, resistance, and yearnings. Gathering to witness invisible footprints and evanescent potentialities, the performance initiates at the fringe of a six-meter recycled plastic curtain featuring a sunken sun and a protruding moon, forming a constellation for what is yet to be born. The participating performers are Maissa Alameldine, Mariamme Boctor, rana elnemr, Nour Kamel, and Farida Rehab. Attendance requires a valid admission ticket to Biennale Arte 2026.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | ZIAD ANTAR | Bladder Diplomacy - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Ziad Antar Presents Bladder Diplomacy Lecture Performance at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Scheduled for Biennale Arte 2026, Bladder Diplomacy weaves together international diplomacy, agricultural habits in the eastern Mediterranean, and personal family stories through a satirical performance.
articles.content: La Biennale di Venezia hosts the lecture performance Bladder Diplomacy at Tese dei Soppalchi on 18 November 2026, running from 16:00 to 17:20. The event weaves stories of international diplomacy and the cultivation of potatoes and tomatoes in the eastern Mediterranean together with personal family narratives. The work examines radical interventions in the natural environment and nutritional habits introduced to the region by modernization and globalized agribusiness. Lebanese artists Ziad Antar, Hatem Imam, and Nayla Mabsout collaborate on the performance, drawing a satirical puzzle of malicious weeds, civil wars, and the resilience of indigenous seeds. The script is written by Ziad Antar, directed by Hatem Imam, and features video by Nayla Mabsout, with Ziad Antar and Nayla Mabsout performing. Visitors must hold a valid admission ticket to Biennale Arte 2026 in order to attend the scheduled event.

articles.originalTitle: Biennale Arte 2026 | CLARISSA HERBST & DOMINIQUE RUST | Whiteout - La Biennale di Venezia
articles.title: Clarissa Herbst and Dominique Rust Present Whiteout Performance at Biennale Arte 2026
articles.excerpt: Dominique Rust and Clarissa Herbst, alongside Michael Wolf, present the Whiteout performance at Sala d’Armi E during Biennale Arte 2026.
articles.content: Scheduled for 17 November 2026 from 14:00 to 14:45 at Sala d’Armi E, the performance titled Whiteout is presented as part of Biennale Arte 2026. The performance utilizes the Duchampian concept of the inframince to explore boundary states between bodies, cultural entities, and moments in time. Dominique Rust and Clarissa Herbst, alongside Michael Wolf, have collaborated for many years on performance projects that combine scripted elements with improvisation. Whiteout was developed within the context of Rust and Herbst’s project for In Minor Keys at Casetta Scaffali within the Arsenale. The installation revisits Parfumerie, an artist-led urban experiment held in Zurich in the late 1980s. Comprising mostly illegal and ad hoc club nights, Parfumerie previously established a space for collective joy. The event features performers Dominique Rust and Michael Wolf, scenography and video by Clarissa Herbst, and music composition by Martin Schütz. Visitors must hold a valid admission ticket to Biennale Arte 2026 to attend.

articles.originalTitle: Loro Piana Celebrates Finest Cashmere, Stages Exhibition - WWD
articles.title: Loro Piana Celebrates Finest Cashmere and Stages New York Exhibition
articles.excerpt: Loro Piana celebrates cashmere with a fineness of 12.89 microns through the 2025 Cashmere Award held at The Brant Foundation in New York, alongside the Master of Cashmere exhibition.
articles.content: Held at The Brant Foundation in New York, the 2025 Loro Piana Cashmere of the Year Award honored fiber with a fineness of 12.89 microns. The event also unveiled the Master of Cashmere exhibition, highlighting the brand's history and manufacturing expertise. Deputy chairman Pier Luigi Loro Piana stated that his journey in China began in the 1980s, building strong trust-based relationships with local communities. Chief executive officer Frédéric Arnault emphasized that cashmere lies at the heart of the brand's identity. The 11th edition of the award honored three couples of cashmere herders from Inner Mongolia, with the first prize bestowed for a fiber diameter of 12.89 microns. Loro Piana carries out various initiatives to strengthen the ecosystem and combat desertification in Mongolia. The company also inaugurated a new knitwear facility in Ghemme, Italy, in September.

articles.originalTitle: About the Punk to Pop exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Exhibition Explores Cultural Transformation from Punk to Pop
articles.excerpt: V&A South Kensington prepares to launch a comprehensive exhibition examining the explosion of music, art, and fashion between 1972 and 1985 in March 2027.
articles.content: Opening on 13 March 2027 at V&A South Kensington, the Punk to Pop exhibition re-examines the creative explosion across music, art, and fashion from 1972 to 1985. Spanning three acts and approximately 300 objects, the showcase traces a historical trajectory starting from glam rock and disco, moving through underground subcultures like punk, Goth, and New Romantics, and concluding with digital-era pop culture. Featuring prominent acts such as Sex Pistols, Grace Jones, Blondie, Joy Division, and Wham!, the exhibition demonstrates how self-determined artists responded to political turbulence and austerity. Highlighted items include album artwork by Jamie Reid, handwritten lyrics by Ian Curtis, Mick Jones's first guitar, and photographs by Andy Warhol. Through theatrical staging, fashion, and stage costumes, the multi-sensory presentation celebrates how music provided a platform for individuality, sexuality, and cultural experimentation during a transformative era.

articles.originalTitle: Probably by Camille Corot | Staircase in the Villa of Maecenas, Tivoli | L814 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Tivoli Landscape Attributed to Camille Corot at the National Gallery
articles.excerpt: A work thought to be by French artist Camille Corot from around 1826 in Italy is held in the National Gallery collection, featuring architectural sections and light contrasts.
articles.content: French artist Camille Corot produced 200 drawings and 150 oil studies during his stay in Italy between 1825 and 1828. Due to the scarcity of signatures on these sketches, attributions remain uncertain. The work titled Staircase in the Villa of Maecenas, Tivoli presents a visually satisfying vista from giant doors towards light coming through upper windows. Tivoli, a town northeast of Rome, was a frequent destination for artists due to its dramatic landscape. While signed Corot on the lower right, the sketch also bears the signature Granet in a likely more recent hand. Measuring 29.7 by 21.5 centimetres, the oil on paper laid on canvas is part of the Gere Collection on long-term loan to the National Gallery and is not currently on display. Corot's dedication to close observation of nature significantly influenced the later Impressionist approach to landscape painting.

articles.originalTitle: Edgar Degas | Promenade beside the Sea | L819 - The National Gallery, London
articles.title: Edgar Degas Painting Promenade beside the Sea at The National Gallery
articles.excerpt: Edgar Degas's early oil sketch Promenade beside the Sea, created around 1860 and depicting the Bay of Naples, is held at The National Gallery in London.
articles.content: Created around 1860 by Edgar Degas, Promenade beside the Sea stands as an early oil sketch exploring the recurrent theme of horses and riders. The artwork depicts an elegantly attired couple on horseback riding along a coastal route towards cliffs. A gentleman in black with a top hat and a lady sitting side-saddle in a dark riding habit make their way past coastal vegetation. The setting has been identified as the Bay of Naples, a location Degas visited during trips to see his Italian family. Open brushwork conveys the movement of the horses' gait, while impasto captures the energy of breaking waves. Measuring 22.5 by 32.5 centimeters, the oil on canvas is on long-term loan from the Gere Collection to The National Gallery in London, cataloged under inventory number L819. Evidence indicates the left-hand section derives from a notebook sketch housed in Paris. The composition reflects the artist's lifelong interest in movement and motion prior to the emergence of the Impressionist group.

articles.originalTitle: About the Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires exhibition - Victoria and Albert Museum
articles.title: V&A Museum Explores Byzantine and Ottoman Legacy in Major Exhibition
articles.excerpt: The Victoria and Albert Museum is hosting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition exploring 1,600 years of artistic production from AD 330 to 1922.
articles.content: V&A South Kensington in London is presenting Constantinople to Istanbul: One City, Two Empires, an exhibition spanning the period from AD 330 to 1922. The exhibition examines the art and design traditions of both the Byzantine and Ottoman empires, highlighting their creative legacy that shaped the Mediterranean and beyond. Spread across four main sections, the exhibition features over 200 objects, including rare decorative arts, fine silks, textiles, ceramic tiles, mosaics, precious metalwork, jewelry, sculpture, architectural furnishings, manuscripts, and paintings. The first section, Roman Beginnings, explores the refounding of the city in AD 330 as the capital of the Roman Empire under Constantine the Great, focusing on its infrastructure and the Hippodrome. Heaven and Earth, the second section, explores how art and architecture served Christianity. Power and Reach examines how the Ottoman court projected authority through visual spectacle and luxury materials, while the final section, Life in the City, investigates the city's cosmopolitan character, religious coexistence, and 19th-century shifts in style. The exhibition remains open until 9 May 2027.

articles.title: Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse Wins Recognition
articles.excerpt: Built in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family courts into a central location.
articles.content: Situated in Newark, the 266,000-square-foot, eight-story Essex County Wynona Lipman Family Courthouse consolidates previously dispersed family and children courts, probation services, and domestic violence units into a central urban location. The primary public entry is carved out under the upper floors to form a plaza as an extension of the streetscape. According to the submission, family courts require a de-escalating environment, addressed here by a multicolor art-glass two-story translucent screen on the public street wall and separate child-friendly playrooms in waiting areas. Constructing the massive complex in downtown Newark required meticulous coordination, including working within strict property lines, managing daily traffic flows, and minimizing disruptions to neighbors. The interior design divides spaces to separate hostile parties while accommodating sensitive zones, and integrates modern security with separate private entry points, holding cells, secure sallyports, and underground parking for judges. To counter unpredictable conditions, the project team relied on daily meetings and constant communication, allowing project managers, superintendents, and safety managers to address obstacles, coordinate daily tasks, and adapt in real time alongside cooperation with the city of Newark.
